card: This PR refactors block validation methods including CheckBlock, AcceptBlock, FlushStateToDisk, and ProcessNewBlockHeaders to return BlockValidationState by value rather than taking an out-parameter alongside a boolean return code. It eliminates the risk of divergence between boolean status codes and the inner validation state, preventing state leakage across chained calls. The change was requested during the review of PR 33856 to clean up internal validation semantics and kernel interfaces. It has no external dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor commit refinements; the overall approach and set of 12 commits remain unchanged.
evidence: PR description: 'Exclude the potentially inconsistent case when the bool return value and the returned state are inconsistent' and 'Remove the possibility of unintuitive interaction between subsequent calls with the same state.'
PR description links to review discussion on #33856 where follow-up refactoring of validation return conventions was requested.
problem: Validation functions returned a bool while writing to a mutable BlockValidationState out-parameter. This allows the boolean return value and the validation state to disagree, creates ambiguity about whether an incoming state is read or overwritten, and risks state pollution across chained calls where an existing error state prevents a new failure reason from being recorded.

risk.why: A mistake in handling return state across block or header acceptance could inadvertently treat invalid blocks as valid or reject valid headers, risking consensus divergence or peer banning.

scope_notes: Touches critical validation and consensus-checking logic across 12 granular commits ordered bottom-to-top in the call hierarchy, including kernel C API and fuzz target updates.
summary: Refactors block and header validation functions in validation.cpp and validation.h to return BlockValidationState by value instead of using an out-parameter with a bool return value. Introduces MakeInvalid and MakeError static helper methods on BlockValidationState to construct failure states inline. Callers across net_processing, the kernel C API, RPC, tests, and benchmarks are updated accordingly.
